stem: Why do unannounced session timeouts on web forms create significant barriers for people with cognitive disabilities?

options.text: Users need extra time to read prompts and enter responses, which timers erase on timeout.
options.shortLabel: Need extra time without losing work
options.rationale: Users with cognitive or learning disabilities often need extended time to comprehend instructions and complete complex inputs without sudden data loss.

options.text: Users rely on spellcheck and predictive text, which timers disable them on timeout.
options.rationale: Session timers track inactivity; they do not disable browser spellcheck or predictive text tools.

options.text: Users depend on visible focus indicators to track their place, which timers hide on timeout.
options.rationale: Having a session timeout does not remove focus indicators or alter how form fields are visually styled.

options.text: Users often use text-to-speech tools, which timers block from reading form labels aloud.
options.rationale: Text-to-speech software reads page content aloud and is not blocked by background session timers.

explanation: Individuals with cognitive, learning, or reading disabilities often require more time to comprehend written prompts, gather information, and input form data. Sudden session expirations that wipe out entered data cause stress and make completion impossible unless users can extend the time limit or resume saved work.

references.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding Docs: Understanding SC 2.2.6 Timeouts
